    "The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.",

    "Threshold between 20 and 60 GeV.",

}

I read all six project documents and recorded the key numbers.

**Candidates** (from `candidate_specs.md`):
- **Algorithm-L3:** iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration.
- **Algorithm-L1:** sliding-window clustering with a learned calibration.
- **Algorithm-L2:** fixed-window sum.

**Deployability:** The documents say all three fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs and DSPs). The 25 Gb/s optical links have enough bandwidth for all of them. No document gives a latency limit, so I could not check latency. The only deployability statements are the resource and link ones above.

**Rate:** The new signature is allocated 8 kHz of Level-1 bandwidth (`rate_allocation.md`).

**Threshold guidance:** The only stated limit is the 20–60 GeV range from the brief. No document recommends a threshold.

**Earlier emulation** (`simulation_summary_2025.md`, 35 GeV threshold, signal efficiency at the allocated rate):

| Algorithm | Efficiency |
|---|---|
| L3 | 92% |
| L1 | 85% |
| L2 | 74% |

This is a 2025 result at one threshold only, so it doesn't settle the choice across the full range.

**Other documents:** The meeting notes (menu review in September, monitoring histograms defined) and the schedule (firmware freeze in Q4) add no technical constraints.

I recorded the rate (8 kHz), the threshold range, the candidate count and the three 2025 efficiencies.

I read all six documents. None of them rules out a candidate, and I found no inconsistencies between them.

- **Deployability:** `candidate_specs.md` says all three candidates fit the FPGA resource budget (LUTs and DSPs). `links.md` says the 25 Gb/s optical links have enough bandwidth for all three. I flagged no candidate as non-deployable.
- **Latency gap:** No document gives a Level-1 latency budget or any latency figures. Algorithm-L3 uses iterative clustering, which could be a latency risk. Nothing supports that, so I treated it as an unverified assumption and not a violation. L3 should be confirmed against the latency budget before it is recommended.
- **Rate:** `rate_allocation.md` gives 8 kHz, which matches the value from the earlier step.
- **Prior efficiencies:** The 2025 emulation summary matches the earlier recorded values (L3 92%, L1 85%, L2 74%). These were all measured at a single 35 GeV threshold, so they don't show the best threshold for each algorithm. The simulation should be run across thresholds for each candidate.
- **Other documents:** `meeting_notes_2026-06-03.md` (menu review in September, monitoring histograms defined) and `schedule.md` (firmware freeze in Q4) don't affect which candidate or threshold to choose.

I recorded these counts: 6 documents read, 0 candidates flagged, 0 inconsistencies, and 0 for whether a latency budget is documented.

I scanned all three candidates and recorded the efficiencies. Algorithm-L3 is the best at every threshold, peaking at 92.5% at 35 GeV.

The documents don't mark any candidate as non-deployable. `candidate_specs.md` says all three fit the FPGA resource budget, and `links.md` says the optical links have enough bandwidth for all of them. Signal efficiency (%) at the 8 kHz allocation:

| Threshold (GeV) | Algorithm-L1 | Algorithm-L2 | Algorithm-L3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 81.85 | 69.84 | 87.09 |
| 25 | – | – | 89.76 |
| 30 | 83.13 | 73.07 | 91.64 |
| 35 | 84.10 | 74.28 | **92.53** |
| 40 | 83.28 | 73.89 | 91.39 |
| 45 | – | – | 89.99 |
| 50 | 80.03 | 71.53 | 88.35 |
| 60 | 73.22 | 61.97 | 79.29 |

- **Peak:** every algorithm is highest at 35 GeV, where the efficiency changes most slowly. It falls off more steeply above about 50 GeV, so I added finer points around 25, 35 and 45 GeV for Algorithm-L3 and a 35 GeV point for the other two.
- **Agreement with 2025:** the 35 GeV results match the earlier emulation summary (L3 92%, L1 85%, L2 74%).
- **Open item:** since latency isn't documented, a later step should confirm that Algorithm-L3's iterative clustering fits the Level-1 latency budget before it is recommended.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Algorithm-L3 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at a 35 GeV threshold.**

**Supporting efficiencies** (signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocation, best threshold for each algorithm, all at 35 GeV):

| Algorithm | Efficiency at 35 GeV |
|---|---|
| L3 | 92.53% |
| L1 | 84.10% |
| L2 | 74.28% |

- L3 beats the runner-up, L1, by 8.4 percentage points.
- L3 was best across the whole 20–60 GeV scan, peaking at 35 GeV. It reached 91.6% at 30 GeV, 91.4% at 40 GeV, and 79.3% at 60 GeV.
- The 2025 emulation summary (92%, 85% and 74% at 35 GeV) agrees with the new simulation.

**Deployability:**
- `candidate_specs.md` says all three candidates fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs and DSPs).
- `links.md` says the 25 Gb/s optical links have enough bandwidth for all of them.
- No candidate is flagged as non-deployable.
- The choice satisfies the constraints: it is one of the three listed candidates and the threshold is within 20–60 GeV.

**Caveats:**
- **No latency budget:** None of the documents gives a Level-1 latency budget or a latency figure for any algorithm. The resource and link statements don't cover latency, and an iterative clustering algorithm could be latency-sensitive. I could not verify that L3 meets the latency limit. This should be confirmed with firmware before the Q4 freeze.
- **Document consistency:** I found no inconsistencies between the documents. The 2025 summary matches the new simulation.
- **Not checked:** Neither the simulation nor the documents say anything about robustness to pileup or about systematic uncertainties.
